Rashi on the lemma ונפש כי תקריב: nefesh is said of no freewill offering but the meal-offering; who usually volunteers one? the poor man; God counts it as though he offered his soul (he cites Menachot 104b but prints and adopts it). Ibn Ezra (On Your Way) on the same lemma: nefesh means a person, named because the meal-offering is a freewill gift and the soul too is called willing (Psalm 51:14). Both paraphrases carried by the Hebrew without drift; ‘reads nefesh as the poor man’ compresses Rashi’s why-this-word argument but stays within it. The two differ in the reason for the word and are named without resolution. Locator 2:1 right for both. Plain sense checked in day.js: Leviticus 1 ends the burnt-offerings (1:17), 2:1 opens the meal-offering of fine flour; no four-word run from the key. verse.js ok (Leviticus 2:1, at [91,1]); entry-check ok. Two editions named in src. No school, comparison or tone issue.
